answer.part: How is rule determined, including ordinary ties, Eyrie ties, tokens and the Vagabond pawn?
answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing with more total warriors plus buildings than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means nobody rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop another player ruling.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Rule (2.5)

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: What makes a normal move legal, can the same warriors move repeatedly, and do rivers count as paths?
answer.ruling: Move a positive number of your warriors or pawns along a linking path from one clearing to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces can move repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Move (4.2)

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: Describe battle from ambush through removal: foiling, early ending, dice limits, extra hits, removal priorities and who scores removed buildings/tokens.
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing where you have warriors or the pawn and an enemy to be defender; rule is not required. Defender may play a matching ambush (bird wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise defender deals two immediate hits, not limited by its warriors, and discards the card. If no attacking warriors/pawns remain, battle ends. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have them), roll (higher die is attacker's hits, lower defender's; ties equal; each side's rolled hits capped by its warriors in battle; Alliance defender reverses dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords), then after-roll effects (attacker orders if both have them). Count hits by adding extra hits, subtracting ignored hits, and adding one defenseless hit if defender has no warriors (Vagabond instead checks for no undamaged swords). Each hit removes one opposing piece. Hit recipient chooses removal order and removes all warriors before buildings/tokens; that side orders its piece-removal effects. Both sides deal counted hits, and warrior losses do not change rolled caps retroactively. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores one VP each, including defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Battle (4.3)

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Battle (4.3)

answer.part: How do crafting costs, repeat use of crafting pieces, absent supply items and duplicate persistent effects work?
answer.ruling: For Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance, activate one matching crafting piece per card icon; its suit is its clearing's suit, and each piece may activate only once per turn. Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon; its current clearing must match every icon. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit. An item card cannot be crafted if its matching item token is absent from map supply. An identical persistent effect already in your play area cannot be crafted.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Craft (4.1)

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Craft (4.1)

answer.part: When and at what VP can you activate dominance, what wins each suit, and can an activated card be replaced or discarded?
answer.ruling: During your Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings matching mouse, rabbit, or fox dominance, or (bird dominance) two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. You cannot remove or replace an activated dominance card.

answer.part: What happens to a dominance card spent for suit, and how can another player take it, especially a bird dominance card?
answer.ruling: Whenever a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance into hand. An available bird dominance remains bird, so it requires a bird card; a bird hand card can pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking and activating are separate actions and neither uses a faction action allowance.

answer.part: For standard two-player setup, what deck change, hand size, ruins/item setup and faction setup order apply?
answer.ruling: Remove all four dominance cards with two players, shuffle the shared deck, and deal each player three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is present, put one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, shuffle the stacks to hide identities, then return them to empty R slots; without Vagabond ruins contain no items. Standard setup chooses factions, randomly determines starting player and seating, sets score markers to 0, then sets up factions in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond order. Setup order is distinct from turn order.
answer.evidence: Setup → Standard Setup steps 1–7; Hidden ruin items; faction setup subsections

answer.part: What does the Keep forbid or permit, how do Field Hospitals work, and can the Keep be rebuilt?
answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. Without a Keep, Hospitals have no destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep; Field Hospitals

answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep; Field Hospitals

answer.part: State Marquise Daylight order, action allowance, March moves, Recruit limit and Overwork cost.
answer.ruling: First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit. A Battle is one battle. March is up to two moves and is one compound action that cannot be interrupted to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and may be used only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there.

answer.part: How does the Marquise build, including rule, wood network, track selection and scoring?
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the cost atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the newly uncovered space. You need the full wood cost, available building, and legal slot.

answer.part: State Eyrie Birdsong steps and the no-roost recovery placement requirement.
answer.ruling: In order: Emergency Orders (if hand is empty, draw one); Add to Decree (add one or two hand cards, at most one bird, each to any column); A New Roost. If no roosts are on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

answer.part: How does the Eyrie resolve its Decree, including action suit locations, within-column order and Build restrictions?
answer.ruling: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by columns Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; choose card order freely within each column. Recruit matches a clearing with a roost and places one warrior at one chosen roost there (Charismatic places two). Move matches the origin and requires moving at least one warrior under ordinary path/rule requirements. Battle matches the battle clearing and initiates a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build matches the target clearing and places one roost in a clearing Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. Bird cards are wild in every column, but other action requirements still apply. If any required action cannot be fully completed, Turmoil starts immediately; no skipping or continuing other columns.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight — resolve the Decree

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight — resolve the Decree

answer.part: What exactly happens in Turmoil, including Viziers, leaders, pieces on map and the rest of the turn?
answer.ruling: Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none are face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. End Daylight, then take the normal Evening: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Turmoil, in order; Evening, even after turmoil

answer.part: When does Outrage trigger, what is paid, and what if the player has no matching card or the supporter stack is full?
answer.ruling: Another player triggers Outrage each time they remove sympathy or move any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. They add one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card, they show their hand to Alliance and Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If the Supporters stack is full, discard the incoming card; the payment or no-match draw still occurs. Merely battling there does not trigger unless sympathy is removed.

answer.part: How do Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy differ in timing/order, eligible clearing, supporter cost, martial law and results?
answer.ruling: In Birdsong, complete all Revolts before starting Spread Sympathy; each can be done any number of times, and after spreading starts you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong. For either, each supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild. Revolt targets a sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on the Alliance board; spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP for each enemy building/token removed, place the matching base, place warriors equal to matching-suit sympathetic clearings (including that clearing), and one warrior in Officers. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead. Resolve maximum possible placements if short. Spread Sympathy targets an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; spend the supporters shown above its next token. Add one matching supporter for Martial Law if the target has at least three warriors of one other player. Place sympathy and score its uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep's placement ban still applies.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong; Revolt; Spread Sympathy

answer.part: How does Alliance train officers and organize, and what does losing a base do to supporters/officers?
answer.ruling: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Each officer enables one Evening military operation and is not consumed by taking it. Organize is one operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score the uncovered VP; it uses no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law cost, but placement must be legal. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, birds included, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight; Evening operations

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight; Evening

answer.part: How do Vagabond refresh, Slip, normal Move and forest Rest work, including hostile destinations and Evening drawing?
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh first counts tea already face up on the Refresh track: flip two exhausted items per such tea, then three more; tea refreshed now gives no extra refresh. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, including into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of the origin. Vagabond Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can go only to an adjacent clearing. Evening in a forest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if possible. This Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on its track, even after Rest, then discards to five and checks capacity.

answer.part: How do Vagabond Explore, Quest and Repair work, including costs, rewards and item sides?
answer.ruling: Explore: exhaust a torch in a ruin's clearing, take one hidden item face up into Satchel or a track, score one VP if an item is taken, and remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing its slot. Quest: in a matching-suit clearing, choose a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items, and put it in play completed; choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards, then draw a replacement quest. No cards pay quest cost. Repair: exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space. Damaging preserves face; Repair doesn't itself say to flip an item face up.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight: Explore, Quest, Repair; Pawn and items

answer.part: When does a faction become Hostile to Vagabond, when is Infamy scored, can Aid undo Hostility, and what does Strike target?
answer.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except for the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. During battle on Vagabond's own turn, Infamy gives one extra VP per Hostile piece removed, excluding the warrior that first caused Hostile status; it applies whether Vagabond attacks or defends, not on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship out of Hostile, though Vagabond can still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there can Vagabond remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

answer.part: What are coalition eligibility, timing, VP requirement, partner selection and victory, and what changes if partner is Hostile?
answer.ruling: With four or more players, during Vagabond's Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card to coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; choose among tied candidates. Put Vagabond's score marker on that player's faction board and stop scoring. Vagabond wins if the partner wins, including by dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: Which rules take precedence among cards, Law, Learning to Play and faction rules, and can an ordinary card override a cannot?
answer.ruling: Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. General and faction rules should be followed together when possible, but faction rules win if incompatible. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden; the summary does not give ordinary cards a general power to override it.

answer.part: Who chooses unclear simultaneous resolutions, and may you interrupt a March between its two moves to take another action or spend a bird?
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. In battle, attacker chooses order for effects at the same timing; each side receiving hits orders effects triggered by removal of its pieces. A Marquise March's two moves form one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.
answer.evidence: Turn Structure; Marquise Daylight, March; Battle (4.3)

answer.part: What do at-start and at-end phase timings mean, and can you take ordinary Daylight actions after beginning the last step of your turn?
answer.ruling: “At start” effects precede all other effects in that phase; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

answer.part: What hand/deck/pile information can players inspect or reveal, and may non-binding deals transfer cards or require consent?
answer.ruling: Hand size is public, contents are private and may be shown only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles can be searched or inspected; the deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding, cards can be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases → Cards / hand information

answer.part: What happens immediately when shared deck empties, and how do bird substitutions work for forced non-bird discards versus explicit bird costs?
answer.ruling: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. When instructed to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, birds must be treated as that suit, with the instruction determining how many cards. A non-bird cannot substitute when the instruction explicitly requires bird.

answer.part: If instructed to place more pieces than remain, can you use proxies or choose to place fewer than available, and does shortage waive costs or Eyrie obligations?
answer.ruling: Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If you cannot place all prompted pieces, place the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily place fewer. This does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not waive the Eyrie's duty to complete Decree actions; an incomplete required action causes Turmoil.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Eyrie → Decree

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Eyrie Dynasties

answer.part: Where do placed and removed pieces normally come from/go, what happens to removed items, and when do effects of simultaneous removals trigger?
answer.ruling: Placement normally takes pieces from supply or the leftmost track space. Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces go to the rightmost empty track space. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. For simultaneous removals, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Special Rules & Edge Cases → Place/remove/replace

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Special Rules & Edge Cases

answer.part: When a player is forced to move or battle, whose restrictions/abilities and battle decisions apply?
answer.ruling: Resolve a forced action as if the affected player chose it, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

answer.part: Can an enemy replace a piece in the Keep clearing, and how is a swap different from a move or place?
answer.ruling: No. Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible, and the Keep's ban on others placing there cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move and place restrictions.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases → Place/remove/replace; Marquise → Keep

answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases; Marquise de Cat

answer.part: When two players simultaneously reach 30 VP, who wins?
answer.ruling: The tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player if applicable.

answer.part: How do forest adjacency and Winter river affect Vagabond Slip, and does Fall add any special map rule?
answer.ruling: Forest adjacency follows map rules; on Winter the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Vagabond Slip can move to an adjacent clearing or forest, with forest adjacency determined by those rules. Fall has no special rules.
answer.evidence: Setup; Shared movement → forest definition; Vagabond → Birdsong Slip

answer.part: Give Marquise standard starting placements and supplies, including its unoccupied corner and building-track arrangement.
answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner, then one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

answer.part: Give Eyrie standard starting placements, leader/Vizier procedure and remaining roost arrangement.
answer.ruling: Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep the others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed for that leader. Fill the roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

answer.part: What does Alliance start with in supply, on its board, in hand/supporters, and on the map?
answer.ruling: Supply 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from the player's three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.part: Describe Vagabond setup other than hidden ruin items: pawn, quests, relationships and marked starting items.
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the character's listed S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box. Put each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent.

answer.part: What Reach totals and base-faction values guide choosing two-, three- and four-player mixes?
answer.ruling: Recommended reach totals are at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base reach is Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law permits any adventurous mix totaling at least 17.

answer.part: When and how much wood does Marquise produce, what limits production, and how does its Evening draw work?
answer.ruling: In Birdsong, place one wood at each sawmill, including one per sawmill if multiple share a clearing. Each Overwork action in Daylight also places one wood at a sawmill by spending a card matching that clearing. Both draw from the finite supply of eight wood tokens. In Evening, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard down to five.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Wood production; Birdsong; Evening

answer.part: If Marquise Recruit has more eligible recruiters than available warriors, what is placed and who chooses where?
answer.ruling: Place the maximum warriors available among the eligible recruiters; Marquise chooses which recruiters receive them. Recruit is still limited to once per turn.

answer.part: How do Eyrie item crafting and its Builder leader interact with printed VP and extra crafting-point effects?
answer.ruling: Eyrie normally scores one VP for a crafted item instead of its printed VP under Disdain for Trade. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade. Other extra crafting-point effects still apply.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Lords of the Forest; Disdain for Trade; leader table

answer.part: For each Eyrie leader give the Vizier columns and special ability.
answer.ruling: Builder: Viziers in Recruit and Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit places two warriors instead of one. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, scores one extra VP in addition to normal removal points.

answer.part: If Charismatic must Recruit but only one Eyrie warrior remains in supply, can placing that one fulfill the Decree?
answer.ruling: No. Charismatic's Recruit must place two warriors at one chosen roost in a matching clearing. If the required action cannot be fully completed because of warrior supply, immediately enter Turmoil; do not skip the card or continue other Decree columns.

answer.part: Does Alliance Guerrilla War bypass warrior limits, and how are the dice assigned when Alliance defends?
answer.ruling: No; warrior caps still apply. When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and attacker uses the lower die.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Guerrilla War; Battle → Roll

answer.part: Can Alliance craft from Supporters, inspect them, or count them toward its five-card hand limit?
answer.ruling: Supporters can be inspected by Alliance and spent only for suit; they are not hand cards and do not count toward hand limit. Alliance crafts from hand, not Supporters.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Guerrilla War / Supporters; Daylight Craft

answer.part: Can Alliance first Spread Sympathy into a clearing and then Revolt there in that same Birdsong?
answer.ruling: No. All Revolts must be completed before beginning Spread Sympathy. Once spreading starts, Alliance cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot enable a same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.part: Do two enemy players each having two warriors trigger Martial Law when spreading sympathy, and does Martial Law increase Organize cost?
answer.ruling: No. Martial Law adds one matching supporter only when the target has at least three warriors of one other player; two players with two each do not meet that stated condition. Organize has no Martial Law cost and spends no supporters.

answer.part: Does placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing or moving only Vagabond pawn there cause Outrage, and what if allied warriors accompany Vagabond?
answer.ruling: Placing warriors there does not trigger Outrage, and moving only the Vagabond pawn there does not trigger it. Outrage is triggered by another player moving warriors into a sympathetic clearing; therefore if allied warriors accompany Vagabond into one, their movement triggers Outrage (one matching card per affected move, not per warrior).
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Outrage; Vagabond → Allied benefits / Move

answer.part: What Alliance Evening operations are available, does using an officer consume it, and when are cards drawn?
answer.ruling: Operations are Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize; take up to the number of officers, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board and are not consumed. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.

answer.part: What happens to Vagabond pawn when a revolt or another enemy remove-all-pieces effect hits its clearing?
answer.ruling: The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing all enemy pieces from its clearing instead damages three Vagabond items.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Woodland Alliance → Revolt

answer.part: What determines Vagabond rolled hits and defenseless status, do exhausted swords count, and how are excess hits handled?
answer.ruling: Vagabond's maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Hits damage one undamaged item each; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight Battle; Pawn and items; Battle → Roll/Count

answer.part: How do tea/coins/bags enter or leave item tracks, what is track capacity, and can damaged face-up items pay actions?
answer.ruling: Face-up tea, coins and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each type's track holds at most three. Exhausting an item on a track sends it to Satchel. Repairing a damaged item preserves its current face; when ready, tea/coins/bags move to a track if space. Damaged items cannot pay actions, even if face up; action payment requires a face-up undamaged item.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Repair; item action rule

answer.part: How is Vagabond capacity calculated, what counts toward load, when is it checked and where do excess items go?
answer.ruling: Capacity is six items plus two for each face-up bag on its track. Count items in Satchel plus Damaged box; track items do not count. Check at the end of Evening after drawing and discarding, and permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within capacity. Do not check immediately when acquiring an item.

answer.part: Does forest Rest refresh an undamaged exhausted item, and how does it differ from Refresh or Repair?
answer.ruling: No. Forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if possible; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Birdsong Refresh flips exhausted items face up according to tea on the Refresh track plus three more, without changing damage status. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening Rest

answer.part: What is Vagabond Aid cost and target, is a crafted item required, and how are repeated Aid relationship improvements counted?
answer.ruling: Exhaust one face-up undamaged item of any type and give a card matching the clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items, but no item is required to Aid. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction as many times in the same turn as the number printed between its current and next spaces; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score the new space's VP. At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. Aid cannot advance a Hostile relationship.

answer.part: What changes at Allied status: Aid points, moving warriors and attacking with them, and can you use allied warriors against their own faction?
answer.ruling: Each subsequent Aid to an Allied faction scores two VP. Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany its move; they follow their own movement restrictions, cannot accompany a move specified to be alone, and moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At the start of battle as attacker, Vagabond may treat warriors of one Allied faction there as its own for that battle; they can fight a different enemy, but cannot be used to attack their own faction.

answer.part: When Vagabond takes hits using allied warriors, when and under what comparison does that ally become Hostile?
answer.ruling: In a battle using allied warriors as Vagabond's own, Vagabond may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. If more allied warriors are removed than items damaged in that battle, the ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not trigger it; this special timing overrides ordinary hostility timing for those allied warriors removed as hits against another enemy.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Taking hits with an ally

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Taking hits with an ally

answer.part: Can Vagabond craft a card requiring fox and rabbit icons from one clearing, reuse the pawn for multiple craftings, and immediately use a crafted item?
answer.ruling: No: the pawn's current clearing must match every crafting icon, so one clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit requirements. Vagabond may activate its pawn repeatedly despite the normal once-per-turn crafting limit, but each icon requires its own hammer. When crafting an item, Vagabond may immediately take it face up into Satchel/track and use it for another Daylight action immediately if costs and other requirements are met; the item must be in supply to craft.

answer.part: List base Vagabond characters with starting items and special action costs/results, including Ranger timing.
answer.ruling: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea and sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the Vagabond's clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag and hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow and sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items, keeping their faces, and immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

answer.part: After removing a ruin last item, what happens to its building slot, and can ordinary building placement remove a ruin instead?
answer.ruling: When Explore takes the ruin's last item, remove the ruin and free the building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed, so ordinary building placement cannot remove one.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight Explore; Shared movement → clearings and ruins

answer.part: Can a coalition partner be attacked as an enemy, and does coalition automatically grant Allied relationship powers?
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: A Vagabond battles a previously non-Hostile faction on its own turn, removes two warriors followed by one building. How much removal/Infamy VP, and why?
answer.ruling: The two warriors give 1 Infamy VP total: the first warrior makes that faction Hostile and is excluded, while the second is a Hostile piece removed in battle on Vagabond's own turn. The building gives 2 VP: 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy. Total: 3 VP. Warriors give no ordinary removal VP.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Hostile / Infamy; Scoring → Ordinary removal VP

answer.part: What is the cost of a normal Vagabond move into a clearing with only hostile buildings versus one with hostile warriors from several factions?
answer.ruling: Into a clearing with only Hostile buildings/tokens and no Hostile warriors, exhaust one boot. If it has any warriors of any Hostile faction, exhaust one boot plus one extra boot total, regardless of how many Hostile factions' warriors are present.

answer.part: Does taking an available dominance card activate it immediately, and do taking/activating use a Marquise action?
answer.ruling: No. Taking an available dominance card puts it in hand; activation is a separate action. Neither taking nor activating requires a faction action allowance, including Marquise's.

answer.part: Can ownership of faction pieces change, and are items faction pieces that belong to the faction holding them?
answer.ruling: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possession does not make them faction-owned.

answer.part: What happens to immediate-effect versus persistent crafting cards, and can a card in your play area be spent as though in hand?
answer.ruling: Resolve an immediate-effect card and discard the crafting card to the shared discard pile. Keep a persistent-effect card in your play area and gain its text; it is outside your hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in play.

answer.part: Can ambush or dominance cards be crafted, and what are their other permitted uses?
answer.ruling: Neither can be crafted. An ambush can be played by defender for two immediate hits or by attacker to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. A dominance card can be activated to change the victory condition or spent for suit.
answer.evidence: Actions → Craft; Ambush and Dominance cards

answer.part: In standard setup how are starting player/seating, score markers and dice arranged, and does faction setup order set turn order?
answer.ruling: Determine starting player and seating randomly, put score markers at 0, and place the battle dice nearby. Factions set up in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond letter order; this setup order is distinct from turn order. The summary says turns proceed clockwise.

answer.part: When does the ordinary 30-VP victory take effect: must the player finish the action, phase, or turn first?
answer.ruling: The first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; no action, phase or turn completion is required.

answer.part: What pieces must you have in the clearing to initiate an ordinary battle, whom can you choose as defender, and must you rule that clearing?
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors or Vagabond pawn and an enemy there as defender. Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Battle

answer.part: Who orders both players' before-roll and after-roll battle effects, and who orders effects triggered by a side's pieces being removed?
answer.ruling: When both sides have applicable before-roll effects, the attacker chooses their order; the attacker also orders applicable after-roll effects at the same timing. The side whose pieces are removed chooses the order of effects triggered by their own pieces' removal.

answer.part: In the Count Hits step, how do effects that ignore hits change the total?
answer.ruling: Add extra hits, then subtract hits that are ignored. Defenseless may add one extra hit for the attacker (Vagabond uses its no-undamaged-swords condition).

answer.part: When a non-Vagabond base faction crafts an item, where does that item come from and where is it placed, and what is the usual VP reward?
answer.ruling: The matching item token must be in the map item supply. On crafting, take it from supply into the crafting faction's Crafted Items box and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie's Disdain (one VP instead of printed; Builder ignores it). Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.
answer.evidence: Actions → Craft; Eyrie → Disdain for Trade

answer.part: Which crafting pieces do the Eyrie and Alliance activate, how is a crafting piece's suit determined, and what does a three-color question-mark crafting icon require?
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy, one matching piece for each icon. A crafting piece's suit is the suit of its clearing. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

answer.part: How does Alliance Mobilize work, and must Alliance finish all crafting before mobilizing or training during Daylight?
answer.ruling: Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters. With no base on map, keep at most five supporters and discard incoming overflow; with any base, there is no cap. Alliance may Craft, Mobilize and Train in any order and number during Daylight; it need not finish crafting first.

answer.part: How does the Eyrie score and draw in an ordinary Evening, and does the scoring still happen after Turmoil?
answer.ruling: Score the VP printed on the rightmost empty roost-track space, then draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discard to five. The full normal Evening, including roost scoring and drawing, still happens after Turmoil.

answer.part: What does the Vagabond pay to initiate its Daylight Battle action, and can an exhausted undamaged sword pay that cost merely because it still counts for rolled hits?
answer.ruling: Exhaust one sword to initiate Battle, which requires a face-up undamaged item. An exhausted sword cannot pay the action cost, though an undamaged sword counts toward maximum rolled hits whether face up or face down.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight Battle; Pawn and items

answer.part: What is the order of phases in a turn, and whose turn begins after Evening ends?
answer.ruling: A turn proceeds Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. Turns proceed clockwise, so the next player's turn begins after Evening.

answer.part: When Vagabond takes a hit, which item must be chosen, where does it go, does its face change, and can already-damaged items absorb another hit?
answer.ruling: For each hit, choose one undamaged item; it is placed in the Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit. If no undamaged items remain, excess hits are ignored.

answer.part: During Alliance Evening, how many military operations may be taken, and for one Recruit operation how many warriors are placed and where?
answer.ruling: Take up to the number of officers in military operations, in any order and repetition; officers are not consumed. One Recruit operation places one warrior in one clearing with a base.

answer.part: How many Daylight actions may the Vagabond take, must the action types follow a fixed order, and may the same action type be repeated?
answer.ruling: Vagabond Daylight actions can be taken in any order and number, as ready undamaged items permit; there is no fixed action sequence and action types may be repeated subject to their costs and other requirements.

answer.part: What item and how many of it must the Vagabond exhaust to take the Daylight Strike action, and can an exhausted or damaged copy pay that cost?
answer.ruling: Exhaust one crossbow to take Strike. It must be face up and undamaged to pay; an exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight Strike; Pawn and items
